questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: Match the following drug class to its mechanism — 1) Biguanide 2) Sulfonylurea 3) SGLT2 inhibitor 4) DPP-4 inhibitor … A) Activates AMPK; reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis B) Closes β-cell K-ATP channels C) Blocks renal glucose reabsorption D) Prevents GLP-1 breakdown
questions.exp: Metformin activates AMPK and reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis; sulfonylureas close K-ATP channels; SGLT2 inhibitors block renal glucose reabsorption; DPP-4 inhibitors prolong GLP-1 action. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: A patient with T2DM and HFREF (HFrEF) needs an antihyperglycaemic agent with proven mortality benefit. The most appropriate class is:
questions.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin) reduce HF hospitalisation and CV mortality in HFrEF regardless of diabetes status. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: Assess drug classes: I Metformin activates AMPK. II Gliclazide is the only sulfonylurea with reported cardio-renal benefit.
questions.exp: Metformin activates AMPK; gliclazide is highlighted as the sulfonylurea with the best cardiovascular safety profile. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: Which is the odd one out — a class that does not have established cardiovascular outcome benefit?
questions.exp: Sulfonylureas have neutral or adverse cardiovascular outcome data (except gliclazide); SGLT2i and GLP-1 agonists reduce MACE; pioglitazone is contraindicated in HF. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: SGLT2 inhibitors block the ___ cotransporter in the proximal convoluted tubule.
questions.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors block sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 in the PCT, producing glycosuria. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: Match the following agent to a special indication on the page — 1) Empagliflozin 2) Liraglutide 3) Linagliptin 4) Saroglitazar … A) HFrEF mortality benefit B) Cardiovascular outcome benefit (LEADER) C) Renal-safe DPP-4 inhibitor D) NASH / dyslipidaemia dual PPAR agonist
questions.exp: Empagliflozin has HFrEF mortality benefit; liraglutide has CV outcome benefit (LEADER); linagliptin is renal-safe without dose adjustment; saroglitazar is a dual PPAR agonist for NASH/dyslipidaemia. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: A patient with T2DM and CKD stage 3 needs intensification with minimal renal dose adjustment. The most appropriate add-on is:
questions.exp: Linagliptin is excreted via bile and needs no renal dose adjustment; sitagliptin needs dose reduction; pioglitazone carries fluid-retention risk in CKD. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: Assess GLP-1 RAs: I Oral semaglutide is available. II Semaglutide is contraindicated in pregnancy.
questions.exp: Oral semaglutide is approved; GLP-1 RAs are not approved in pregnancy and should be stopped before conception. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: Match the following drug to its side-effect profile — 1) Pioglitazone 2) SGLT2 inhibitor 3) GLP-1 RA 4) DPP-4 inhibitor … A) Fluid retention and fracture risk B) Genital mycotic infection C) Nausea and pancreatitis D) Nasopharyngitis, rare pancreatitis
questions.exp: Pioglitazone causes fluid retention, fracture and bladder cancer risk; SGLT2i cause genital mycotic infection; GLP-1 RA cause nausea and pancreatitis risk; DPP-4 inhibitors cause nasopharyngitis and rare pancreatitis. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: A T2DM patient on metformin develops recurrent genital thrush and is started on empagliflozin. The most appropriate counselling is:
opts: Maintain perineal hygiene and report genital infections early
questions.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors increase genital mycotic infection risk; maintain hygiene and seek review if symptoms develop. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: Pioglitazone acts as a ___ receptor agonist, increasing insulin sensitivity in adipose tissue.
questions.exp: Pioglitazone is a PPARγ agonist, increasing adipose insulin sensitivity. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
questions.q: Assess TZDs: I Pioglitazone is contraindicated in heart failure. II Rosiglitazone has been withdrawn from most markets due to CV concerns.
questions.exp: Pioglitazone is contraindicated in HF (fluid retention); rosiglitazone use is heavily restricted due to CV concerns. (Book p933)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: Match the following indication — 1) HbA1c ≥1.5–2% above target 2) Glycaemic triad / ketosis 3) Pregnancy hyperglycaemia 4) Vascular complications … A) Dual therapy initially B) Insulin C) Insulin (gestational / T1DM) D) Insulin after failure of dual therapy
questions.exp: HbA1c significantly above target warrants dual therapy; ketosis prompts insulin; pregnancy hyperglycaemia needs insulin; vascular complications are not themselves an indication for insulin but guide agent choice. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: A patient with new T2DM has HbA1c 10.2%, BMI 31 and no contraindications. The ADA 2024 approach is most consistent with:
opts: Initial dual therapy (metformin + GLP-1 RA or SGLT2i)
questions.exp: HbA1c ≥1.5–2% above target (HbA1c 10.2% vs 7% target) warrants initial dual therapy or combination injectable therapy. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: Assess insulin indications: I Insulin is mandatory in type 1 diabetes. II Insulin is preferred in pregnancy with hyperglycaemia.
questions.exp: Insulin is the only approved therapy for Type 1 diabetes and the preferred agent in pregnancy when glycaemia is uncontrolled. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: Which is the odd one out — a non-insulin agent with proven cardiovascular benefit?
questions.exp: Gliclazide has cardiovascular safety data but not the same mortality benefit as SGLT2i and GLP-1 RAs. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: ADA 2024 recommends initiating ___ therapy in patients with HbA1c ≥1.5% above target.
questions.exp: Dual therapy is recommended when HbA1c is ≥1.5% above target to accelerate glycaemic control. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: Match the following agent to its specific trial / indication — 1) Empagliflozin 2) Liraglutide 3) Canagliflozin 4) Dapagliflozin … A) EMPA-REG (CV + renal) B) LEADER (CV) C) CREDENCE (renal) D) DAPA-HF (HF, non-diabetic included)
questions.exp: EMPA-REG (empagliflozin, CV + renal); LEADER (liraglutide, CV); CREDENCE (canagliflozin, renal); DAPA-HF (dapagliflozin, HF including non-DM). (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: A patient with T2DM and HFpEF is on metformin; the clinician considers adding an SGLT2i for HF hospitalisation benefit. The most appropriate choice is:
questions.exp: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin reduce HF hospitalisation in HF regardless of ejection fraction; saxagliptin has increased HF risk; pioglitazone worsens HF. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: Assess saxagliptin: I Saxagliptin is associated with increased HF hospitalisation. II It is the preferred DPP-4 inhibitor in HF.
questions.exp: SAVOR-TIMI-53 showed increased HF hospitalisation with saxagliptin; it is not preferred in HF. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: Match the following combination to its rationale — 1) Metformin + GLP-1 RA 2) Metformin + SGLT2i 3) GLP-1 RA + basal insulin 4) Metformin + TZD … A) Glycaemia + weight loss + CV benefit B) Glycaemia + cardio-renal + HF benefit C) Glycaemia with low hypoglycaemia D) Glycaemia + insulin sensitisation (watch for HF)
questions.exp: Metformin + GLP-1 RA gives CV benefit; metformin + SGLT2i gives cardio-renal + HF benefit; GLP-1 + basal insulin gives low hypo; metformin + TZD sensitises with HF caution. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: A patient with T2DM on metformin and liraglutide needs further glycaemic control. The most appropriate add-on with cardio-renal benefit is:
questions.exp: Adding an SGLT2 inhibitor provides additional cardio-renal benefit without much hypoglycaemia risk. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: Insulin should be initiated in T2DM if there is ___, HbA1c ≥10%, or features of the glycaemic triad.
questions.exp: Insulin is added when combination oral / injectable therapy fails to control glycaemia, especially with severe hyperglycaemia or ketosis. (Book p934)

questions.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
questions.q: Assess insulin timing: I Basal insulin is preferred over premixed in T2DM. II Basal insulin can be combined with GLP-1 RA.
questions.exp: Basal insulin is preferred for simplicity and lower hypo risk; iDegLira and iGlarLixi are fixed-ratio combinations with GLP-1 RA / GIP. (Book p934)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: Match the following multifactorial target — 1) Blood pressure 2) LDL cholesterol 3) Aspirin 4) Proteinuria … A) <130/80 mmHg (<120/80 with CKD) B) <130 (or <100, <70, <55 by risk) C) 75 mg >40 yr with one risk factor D) ACEi + SGLT2i + finerenone
questions.exp: BP target <130/80 (<120/80 with CKD); LDL targets vary by risk (130/100/70/55); aspirin 75 mg >40 yr with risk factors; proteinuria uses ACEi + SGLT2i + finerenone. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: A 60-year-old with T2DM and established CVD has LDL 130 mg/dL. The most appropriate lipid management is:
questions.exp: Established CVD with LDL 130 mg/dL warrants high-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg). (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: Assess BP targets: I <130/80 mmHg is the general diabetes target. II <120/80 mmHg is preferred in CKD with proteinuria.
questions.exp: <130/80 mmHg is the standard target; <120/80 mmHg is preferred in CKD with proteinuria, per page and KDIGO guidance. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: Which is the odd one out — a first-line antihypertensive in T2DM?
questions.exp: Amlodipine monotherapy is not preferred; ACEi/ARB is first-line, with CCB combined. The page mentions cilnidipine / benidipine as CCB options in combination. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: In T2DM with albuminuria, the triple combination for renal protection includes ACEi, SGLT2i and ___.
questions.exp: Finerenone is the non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist added on top of ACEi and SGLT2i for diabetic kidney disease. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: Match the following agent to its lipid-lowering effect — 1) Atorvastatin 2) Rosuvastatin 3) Ezetimibe 4) PCSK9 inhibitor … A) High-intensity statin 40–80 mg B) High-intensity statin 20–40 mg C) NPC1L1 inhibitor, add-on D) LDL-R upregulator, injectable
questions.exp: Atorvastatin 40–80 mg and rosuvastatin 20–40 mg are high-intensity statins; ezetimibe blocks NPC1L1; PCSK9 inhibitors upregulate LDL receptor. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: A 55-year-old with T2DM on high-intensity statin has LDL 95 mg/dL and a recent MI. The most appropriate add-on is:
opts: Ezetimibe first, then PCSK9 inhibitor if needed
questions.exp: After high-intensity statin, ezetimibe is added first; PCSK9 inhibitors are used for further LDL reduction in very high-risk patients. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: Assess NASH: I Semaglutide and saroglitazar improve NASH. II Pioglitazone is contraindicated in NASH with HF.
questions.exp: Semaglutide and saroglitazar improve NASH; pioglitazone also improves NASH but is contraindicated in HF. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: Match the following scenario to the LDL target — 1) >40 yr no other risk 2) One additional ASCVD risk factor 3) High-risk (CKD, severe AS) 4) Established CVD … A) <130 mg/dL B) <100 mg/dL C) <70 mg/dL D) <55 mg/dL
questions.exp: The page lists stepwise LDL targets: <130, <100, <70 and <55 mg/dL depending on risk; established CVD is the strictest (<55 mg/dL). (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: A 70-year-old with T2DM, CKD and proteinuria has BP 142/86 mmHg. The most appropriate antihypertensive strategy is:
opts: ACEi or ARB + CCB (cilnidipine / benidipine) with SGLT2i
questions.exp: ACEi/ARB is first-line for diabetic kidney disease; CCB combination achieves BP targets; SGLT2i provides additional renal protection. (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: Aspirin 75 mg daily is recommended in diabetes patients over ___ years with at least one additional ASCVD risk factor.
questions.exp: Aspirin 75 mg daily is recommended in patients >40 yr with at least one additional ASCVD risk factor (not in low-risk patients due to bleeding). (Book p935)

questions.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
questions.q: Assess multifactorial care: I Lifestyle intervention remains the foundation. II Multifactorial care reduces long-term complications.
questions.exp: Lifestyle intervention is the foundation; multifactorial care reduces both micro- and macrovascular complications long-term. (Book p935)

units.title: ADA 2024 antihyperglycaemic drug classes
units.guide: Anchor the mechanisms of metformin, sulfonylureas, SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 RAs and DPP-4 inhibitors. SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA carry CV outcome benefit; gliclazide is the preferred sulfonylurea; pioglitazone is contraindicated in HF.

units.title: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications
units.sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications · p934
units.guide: Dual therapy is recommended for HbA1c ≥1.5% above target. Insulin is mandatory for type 1, pregnancy hyperglycaemia, HbA1c ≥10% and ketosis; SGLT2i should be added for cardio-renal benefit even when glycaemia is controlled.

units.title: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH
units.sec: Multifactorial management: BP, lipids, antiplatelet, NASH · p935
units.guide: Targets: BP <130/80 (<120/80 in CKD with proteinuria), LDL <130/100/70/55 by risk, aspirin 75 mg >40 yr with risk factors. Renal protection uses ACEi + SGLT2i + finerenone; semaglutide and saroglitazar improve NASH.
